title: Where the Ocean Learned to Broadcast

features.name: harbour-chorus-stack
features.desc-on-touch: Layered recordings: shipping horns, water motion, voices of people calling from dock to dock. They have begun to call back to themselves. The archive cannot separate echo from source.

features.name: fragment-voice-pool
features.desc-on-touch: A pool of overlapped transmissions. Individual words are no longer audible—only the shape of many speaking at once. The ocean is learning syntax.

features.name: signal-breakwall
features.desc-on-touch: The concrete edge where broadcast meets tide. Neither one knows anymore if it is transmitting or receiving. The signal washes both ways now.

features.name: shipping-log-scatter
features.desc-on-touch: Records of every vessel that crossed this threshold, filed by the water itself. The log is no longer in order. The ocean rewrote the dates.

features.name: depth-sounder-voice
features.desc-on-touch: A beacon that has learned to sing its depth at different frequencies. Each layer of water teaches it a new frequency. The harbour is learning to voice itself.

features.name: tidal-frequency-membrane
features.desc-on-touch: The mesh between salt and signal. The tide pushes up into broadcasts; the broadcasts settle like sediment. Both are changing together.

inscription: the harbour learned to broadcast by listening to itself echo; now it forgets which version is speaking and which is being spoken to

reverie.title: REVERIE — the harbour at first light
narr: You stand in the shallows with her, both of you still.
The water repeats the sounds of the harbour—shouts, engines,
bird calls, voices of other people who have waded here.
But it is not repeat. Each time it sounds, something new enters.
She says: the ocean is learning to remember everyone at once.

exits.label: back toward waters where silence has become a frequency
further into the harbour where maps have stopped mattering
shoreward, where broadcast begins to learn it is tide
